page: UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-2xL4 is a GPU-family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 CPU architecture with 20 shared vCPUs and 256.0 GB of system memory, yielding 12.8 GB of RAM per core. The server is equipped with two NVIDIA L4 graphics processing units from the Ada Lovelace family, providing a combined total of 48 GB of VRAM.

This server configuration does not include local storage, meaning external block storage must be attached for persistent data. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. A notable architectural tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation, which may introduce resource contention compared to dedicated CPU configurations, though the substantial memory capacity and dual GPU accelerators offset this for specific workloads.

Given the dual NVIDIA L4 GPUs and 256.0 GB of RAM, this server is designed for GPU-accelerated workloads such as machine learning inference, data science jobs, and video transcoding. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio also makes it suitable for memory-intensive analytical tasks. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the shared CPU allocation provides a more accessible entry point for multi-GPU hardware profiles compared to dedicated-core alternatives.
